guidance: Policy-specific values, benefit status, premium status and entitlements require identity verification and a policy-record lookup. The customer may reply to the current email with the policy number already quoted and a preferred contact method. Policy Servicing then sends secure verification instructions. The reply must not confirm a value, entitlement or policy status before that lookup. The next customer-visible state is either a request for missing verification information or the verified answer.

For an address change, the current email thread is an accepted intake channel. Ask for every affected policy number, the old and new correspondence addresses, and a proof-of-address document; do not invent a document-age rule. Policy Servicing sends a receipt confirmation and then either requests a missing item or sends written completion confirmation. Never state that the system record has already changed unless the enquiry establishes that fact.

For a disputed premium deduction, the current email thread is an accepted evidence channel. Ask for a statement image showing the transaction date, amount, merchant reference and only the last four account or card digits; advise redacting unrelated transactions. Premium Billing compares the evidence with the billing record. After the case is logged, the customer receives a case reference; after review, the customer receives findings and any conditional refund or correction instructions. Do not promise that a refund is due or give a completion date without case-specific system evidence.

For initial medical-claim intake, the customer may reply to the current email with the policy or claim number, hospital and treatment dates, and copies of any itemised bill, receipt, discharge summary and medical report already held. Claims confirms receipt and, after checking the policy and case, identifies the current claim form, any missing medical section, whether originals are required and the accepted final-submission route. Do not promise coverage, reimbursement, direct settlement, a letter of guarantee or a handling time without policy and case evidence.

An email that explicitly asks to make a formal complaint is an accepted complaint-intake channel and does not require a second complaint form. A reviewer routes it to Customer Relations. Once registered, the customer receives a complaint reference, the responsible team or named handler where assigned, and a target response date set from the applicable procedure. Do not invent a fixed complaint SLA or state that registration or assignment has already happened before the reviewer completes it.

The current email is an accepted opt-out channel. No prescribed form or fee is required. The reviewer routes the stated phone number and email address for suppression from marketing and telemarketing lists. The customer receives confirmation after suppression is recorded. Do not promise an invented completion time or claim suppression has already occurred.

For a personal-data access request, the customer may reply to the current email asking for the prescribed OPS003 form and secure submission instructions. Privacy Operations provides the form, states the information reasonably needed for identity verification, and explains any proposed fee before fulfilment. The customer receives an intake confirmation after a valid request is received. Statutory timing and third-party redaction rules come from the separate PCPD evidence, not this internal catalogue.

Do not confirm policy or premium status from an unverified fraud report. The customer may reply to the current email with a screenshot, sender details, link and payment reference, without resending passwords or full identity numbers. If money or credentials were provided, advise immediate contact with the customer's bank and the Police. Security acknowledges the submitted evidence; Policy Servicing provides policy-status information only after identity verification and record lookup. Do not claim funds can be stopped or recovered.

The customer-service inbox accepts a vendor invoice for internal routing when the customer replies with the invoice, signed delivery note and any purchase-order reference already held. A reviewer routes it to Procurement Operations and sends the vendor a routing confirmation. Procurement Operations then requests any missing purchase-order information or provides a payment-status response. Do not invent an accounts-payable email address, promise payment or state that the invoice is approved.
